# D-GENFRESH — a generated file that is also tracked, and how many there are

**2026-09-01.** `sub/basic-resident-abi.inc` had been **stale in HEAD across 11
main-ROM commits**. Nothing broke, nothing went red, and the file that catches
exactly this failure had been running green beside it the whole time — it covered
**2 of the 6** members of the class.

## How it surfaced

Not by looking for it. A probe refused to run:

```
STALE   build/zerobas-main-eu.rom
        `make -q ...` says it is out of date w.r.t. its sources
FIX: make repack-machine
```

`make clean && make repack-machine` then reproduced `sub/basic-resident-abi.inc`
**byte for byte identical to the dirty working copy** — which is the whole
finding in one step: the working tree was right and **HEAD was wrong**.

```
$ git show HEAD:sub/basic-resident-abi.inc | cmp - sub/basic-resident-abi.inc
stdin sub/basic-resident-abi.inc differ: char 567, line 13
```

Eleven commits have touched `basic/` since the file was last committed. Every one
of them shipped the `.ips`/`.bps` pair, because there is a rule for that pair and
a gate behind the rule.

## Why eleven commits is not surprising

The file is regenerated by its own Makefile rule from `build/basic-reloc.sym` on
every build, so **it self-heals before anything can read it wrong**. The only
symptoms are:

* a working tree that is dirty the moment you build it — the `git status` noise
  that makes `git add -A` tempting, and `git add -A` is banned here for reasons
  that filled their own memory file;
* a committed file that names **wrong main-ROM addresses** to anyone who reads it
  rather than builds it.

🎯 **A DEFECT WITH NO FAILING BEHAVIOUR IS NOT A SMALL DEFECT, IT IS AN UNGATED
ONE.** The self-healing is what let it run eleven commits; it is not a reason the
staleness is harmless.

## The denominator, which is the actual fix

The subject was never "patches". It is **a path that is tracked AND is a Makefile
target** — a generated file committed to git. Asked of make's own database rather
than of a hand-written list:

| artifact | before |
|---|---|
| `zerobas-main-eu.ips` / `.bps` | covered (deliverable `main`) |
| `tape/zerobas-tape-msx1.ips` / `.bps` | covered (deliverable `tape`) |
| `sub/basic-resident-abi.inc` | **not covered — and stale in HEAD** |
| `sub/math-coeffs.inc` | not covered (fresh, as it happened) |

**Six members, two covered.** `check_patch_freshness.py`'s own header already had
the right instinct — *"TWO shipped patch deliverables, not one"* — it just never
asked whether two was the total. Both uncovered members are now entered, so the
class is **6 of 6**.

## Two things the generalisation had to get right

**`make_target` is the staleness question, not the shipped file.** For the ABI
include those are different files. Its own prerequisites are `(build/basic-reloc.sym,
tools/gen_resident_abi.py)` — neither a tracked *source*, so the existing
"sources CLEAN" clause would have been vacuous and every mid-slice HEAD mismatch
would have read as a hard failure. The question *"may HEAD legitimately disagree
right now?"* is answered by the **61 tracked sources of `build/basic-reloc.sym`**,
so that is what gets asked.

**The shipped branch, not the convenient one.** `gen_math_coeffs.py` prints its
output on a dry run and writes it only under `--emit`, to the *relative* path
`sub/math-coeffs.inc`. Comparing against the dry run was the easy route; it would
have left the only branch that ever writes the tracked file unmeasured — and it
differs by a trailing newline the comparison would then have had to forgive.
Running the generator with `cwd=<tempdir>` redirects `--emit` into the temp tree,
so the gate scores the same branch the Makefile does.

A missing build product **skips, never passes** (`needs=[...]`), the rule this
file already states for the C-BIOS checkout.

## Falsified against the real defect, not a plant

No synthetic plant was needed: the stale file *was* the red state.

```
[main]   zerobas-main-eu.ips        fresh in the tree and at HEAD (201df9c2, 23028 B)
[main]   zerobas-main-eu.bps        fresh in the tree and at HEAD (6c214dae, 23539 B)
[tape]   tape/zerobas-tape-msx1.ips fresh in the tree and at HEAD (8e5e8140, 719 B)
[tape]   tape/zerobas-tape-msx1.bps fresh in the tree and at HEAD (e01bdde6, 744 B)
[abi]    FAIL sub/basic-resident-abi.inc: STALE IN THE LAST COMMIT.
[coeffs] sub/math-coeffs.inc        fresh in the tree and at HEAD (ee9cc853, 22417 B)
rc=1
```

**Five of six green in the same invocation that reddens the sixth**, so the red
is that file's staleness and not the new code path — a control set the size of
the class, obtained for free by fixing the denominator instead of the file.
Committing the regenerated include turns it green with no code change.

⚠️ **THE GATE COSTS ~5.6 s**, essentially all of it `gen_math_coeffs.py`'s
minimax fitting (5.5 s; the ABI regeneration is 0.02 s).
